payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.

parsed.text:
The graph is structurally close to the right solution: it preserves the sole requirement, has one requested check for the outcome, and distinguishes complete, partial, absent, and unknown. The evaluation’s observation supports a complete chalk-drawing transformation, so there is no clear criterion defect to fix merely to force agreement with the reference label. In particular, do not change the graph to prescribe “partial” or to discount visible chalk-like rendering just because the reference label differs.

The main opportunity is to make the fulfillment criteria more discriminating and grounded in the source/edit comparison. “Visibly rendered as a chalk drawing” is broad enough that a texture or filter could be mistaken for a full transformation. Clarify that completion requires the depicted image as a whole—including the giraffes and surroundings—to read as a chalk-made drawing, with characteristic chalk-like strokes or grain, rather than merely retaining a photographic image with a localized or superficial effect. Keep partial for clear but incomplete chalk treatment, absent for confident evidence of no requested transformation, and unknown for insufficient evidence. Avoid requiring specific colors, composition changes, or other stylistic details not stated in the instruction.

The current target and reference already bind the check to the source and edited images and the requested chalk-drawing appearance. Preserve that binding and the exact R1 text and source quote. Keep one requested check for O1 and no support checks unless a genuine evidence need arises; any support check would have to be used by the requested check and would not itself count as fulfillment. Return the complete three-key graph, since the supplied variable omits requirements and outcomes and is not a valid executable graph under the stated schema.
